# Continual-ARC reusable observation

## Verified resolution: directional L recoloring (task-0fdb20b5)
This task was correctly solved on a 15x29 test after two demos. The input had background 5 and a large color-2 L marker near the upper-right: vertical arm in column 22 at rows 0-5, horizontal arm along row 5 columns 22-28. The only change in the correct output was recoloring the connected color-0 component at rows 2-5, columns 16-18 from 0 to 2; every other cell stayed exactly as input. That component is 3x3 at rows 2-4 (with row 5 columns 16-17) and connected as one object. Preserve the grid dimensions; leave the marker and all other components untouched.

The two demos confirm the general output form: exactly one object changes uniformly into the L marker's color. Demo 1: color-2 L marker, target color-1 component at rows 16-19 cols 5-7 recolored to 2. Demo 2: color-7 L marker, target color-2 object at rows 0-3 cols 0-5 recolored to 7. The target selector was not fully derived from the examples; therefore retain the solved test as ground truth and avoid unsupported shape/position assumptions. In particular, an earlier note below speculated that a color-3 object in the test was the target; that guess was incorrect. The actual target was the connected color-0 component described above.

## L-marker duplicate-shape recoloring (task-0fdb20b5; inferred from demos, unverified test)
Across demos 6 and 7, a long monochrome L-shaped object acts as a directional marker. Find two congruent (rotation/reflection may count) objects, one on each side of the L's corner/arms; recolor the object on the exterior/opposite side of the L's inner quadrant to the L object's color, leaving everything else unchanged. Strong evidence: demo 7 has color-1 L (vertical upward arm at col 4 and horizontal left arm at row 3), two congruent five-cell shapes (color 8 upper-left and color 6 upper-right); output recolors color-6 object to 1 while preserving color 8. Demo 6 similarly recolors the exterior copy of two matching color-5 blobs to color 6. For this task's test, likely candidate pair: color-3 upper-right L-triomino and the same triomino-like subshape embedded in the lower-right color-8 object; the marker is color-2 L with corner at row 6,col 12 and arms extending right/down, so likely recolor the external color-3 upper-right object to 2. This test inference was never validated; prior submissions were wrong, mostly because guesses changed unrelated objects/invalid grid dimensions. Avoid verbose speculation; preserve dimensions and all cells except the single target object.

## Detailed observations: task-0fdb20b5 demos (all eight)
Input/output dimensions are identical in every pair; every pixel is preserved except one connected object, recolored uniformly to the color of a large L-shaped line/bar marker. This is the high-confidence common rule; target selection depends on a geometric relation that was not fully resolved during the instance. Record the differences exactly:
- Demo 1, 24x18, background 3: a small color-6 L triomino at rows 12-13, cols 9-10 (0-indexed) becomes 0. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 2, 26x22, background 9: a 2-cell vertical color-8 domino at rows 1-2, col 14 becomes 2. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 3, 22x27, background 9: four color-1 cells at rows 20-21, cols 2-4 in T/offset shape become 5. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 4, 17x20, background 4: a 4-cell color-1 skewed tetromino at rows 4-5, cols 10-12 becomes 2. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 5, 21x29, background 5: the large connected color-7 region at rows 10-15, cols 13-21 becomes 2. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 6, 19x22, background 7: the large irregular color-5 component at rows 9-11, cols 13-18 becomes 6. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 7, 16x10, background 2: the 5-cell color-6 component near upper-right (rows 2-3, cols 7-9) becomes 1. Other cells unchanged.
- Demo 8, 30x22, background 5: the connected color-4 region at rows 8-14, cols 16-20 becomes 8. Other cells unchanged.

Likely interpretation: the conspicuous L/bar is a color-and-position selector; recolor one separate component with its color (2, 5, 6, 1, 8, etc.). Do not change any part of the L itself or unrelated objects. In the test (11x17), the marker is color 2: horizontal arm row 6, cols 12-16, vertical arm col 12, rows 6-10. Test other components: color 0 blob rows 1-3 cols 7-9; color 3 domino at rows 1-2 cols 13-14 plus separate vertical domino rows 9-10 col 6; color 4 singleton row 10 col 0; color 8 vertical 4x2 block rows 5-8 cols 2-3, vertical 3-cell at rows 6-8 col 10, and lower-right 7-cell component rows 8-10 cols 14-16. Unresolved target is likely selected by geometry/location relative to the L selector, but the instance ended without a correct submission. Previous attempts mostly changed candidate objects based on unsupported template guesses; retain original dimensions and alter only one whole component when applying a future version of this pattern.

## Enclosed-region fill task (task-46e1e7a4; test ended with all 8 attempts wrong)
Rule from demos: keep grid dimensions and walls, recolor with 4 only the background-color cells enclosed by the line color. The line itself is not recolored. Color values vary; fill is consistently 4.

Examples from this instance:
- Demo 1 (13x21; bg=5, wall=1): fill the 2x3 pocket at rows 2-3, cols 3-5 (0-indexed).
- Demo 2 (10x27; bg=8, wall=9): fill 2x3 pockets at rows 4-5, cols 4-6 and cols 16-18.
- Demo 3 (10x13; bg=5, wall=1): fill row 5, cols 1-4.
- Demo 4 (29x21; bg=9, wall=0): fill enclosed rectangles rows 2-3, cols 2-4 and cols 17-19, plus rows 8-9, cols 3-4 and cols 13-14, and rows 8-9, col 18.
- Demo 5 (16x13; bg=1, wall=6): fill rows 2-3, cols 2-4; also rows 9-10, cols 0-4. Note the latter is enclosed against the left grid edge by the wall segments.

Operational rule: flood-fill background from the grid perimeter using 4-neighbor adjacency; convert only unreachable background cells to 4. Preserve all walls and exterior cells. Consider the grid edge as a possible boundary only where the wall arrangement closes a pocket against it; do not assume regions touching an edge are always exterior without tracing openings.

Test input for this instance (20x25; bg=2, wall=8) was submitted incorrectly eight times. A grid can be partitioned by full horizontal/vertical separator lines of a distinctive color. Ignore separators and treat the resulting equal-sized tiles independently. Count occurrences of the tile's non-background/special color; encode the tile as `1` iff the count is exactly 2, otherwise output the background color. Evidence:
- Demo 1: separator color 7, background 2, special 9; separators at row 4 and columns 2,5,8,11 (0-indexed), forming 2x5 tiles each 4x2. Adopt robust observed encoding: in demo1, output 2 for count=1 and 1 for count>=2; in demo2, output 1 for count=2 and 9 for count !=2.
- Validated test: separators color 3 at full rows 3,7 and columns 4,9, creating 3x3 tiles, each 3x4. Background 6, special 5. Tile special-color counts by row: `[2,1,2]`, `[1,2,1]`, `[2,2,2]`. Output was correctly submitted as `[[1,6,1],[6,1,6],[1,1,1]]`; thus for this test the mapping is 1 iff the tile has exactly two 5s, otherwise background 6.

Practical approach: identify full-line separators and crop tiles; use demos to establish the encoding exactly, since rule mapping differed across the two examples above. Avoid guessing output dimensions or treating inputs as a single undivided grid. Preserve no input tile pixels in output; output is a compact matrix of tile classifications.

## Continual-ARC verified rule: uniform constant-grid scaling (task-4b8d2a79; 2026-09-29)
The 2x1 test grid `[[2],[2]]` was correctly transformed to a 6x2 grid consisting entirely of 2s. A single demo had an 6x8 input and 18x16 output, but its multicolor pattern did not directly demonstrate this constant input. Safe verified rule for the observed test: expand a monochrome constant grid of height 2 and width 1 to six rows and two columns, retaining the sole color everywhere. This is task-instance confirmed; the general scale/tile mechanism is not established by the single test. The demo’s output was formed from mirrored/repeated rearrangements, so do not infer an unrestricted general rule from it.

## Continual-ARC verified rule: mirrored triple tiling (task-3fb47f44; 2026-09-29)
The input is an arbitrary H×W grid. Output is 3H×2W. Horizontally, each row becomes its left-right reversal followed by the original row. Vertically, stack three H-row bands in order: input rows reversed, input rows forward, input rows reversed. Thus output[r] = concat(reverse(input[row]), input[row]), where row is selected by the band sequence `[H-1,...,0, 0,...,H-1, H-1,...,0]`. The repeated boundary rows are intentional.

Verified demo: 3×13 input became 9×26 with vertical source-row order `2,1,0,0,1,2,2,1,0`; every output row consists of the corresponding source row reversed then unchanged. Verified test task-3fb47f44: 10×14 input became 30×28 using source-row order `9..0, 0..9, 9..0`, with each source row mirrored-left plus original-right. Submission was confirmed correct.
